name: Warsong Gulch
summary: At the border of Ashenvale and the Barrens, Warsong Gulch is where the Horde and Alliance fight without pause. Warsong orcs cut timber for the Horde, while the night elves of Silverwing Hold defend their sacred forest. Fighters of many races raid the opposing stronghold to seize its banner.

sections.title: Timber and Blood
sections.body: The Horde builds its home in Kalimdor with wood, much of it cut in Ashenvale. The Warsong clan, Grom Hellscream's warriors, have felled trees here since the Horde first landed. Their Warsong Mill at the gulch's end supplies the Horde's camps and walls. The night elves see each fallen tree as a wound to a forest they have guarded for ten thousand years. They also remember that Grom's warriors slew Cenarius in these woods.

sections.title: Outriders and Sentinels
sections.body:
The Horde's fighters are the Warsong Outriders, supplied from Mor'shan Base Camp on the northern edge of the Barrens. There, Kelm Hargunth keeps them armed and fed. The Silverwing Sentinels of Silverwing Hold stand against them.

These night elf warriors are sworn to drive every invader from Ashenvale, and Illiyana Moonblaze supplies them at Silverwing Grove. Allies also flock to the gulch: dwarves and humans beside the Sentinels, and tauren, trolls and Forsaken beside the Outriders.

sections.title: The Struggle for the Banners
sections.body: The Warsong Mill stands at one end of the gulch, and Silverwing Hold at the other. Each stronghold keeps its side's banner. Fighters raid the enemy's hold, seize its flag and race back as defenders hunt them down. Every banner carried home strikes at the enemy's pride. The side that captures the most wins the day.

faq.answer: Warsong Gulch lies in a forested valley between Ashenvale and the Barrens. There, the Horde's Warsong Outriders and the night elves' Silverwing Sentinels fight over the Horde's logging, each trying to capture the other's flag.

faq.q: Why does the Horde fight in Warsong Gulch?
aliases: why do the orcs log ashenvale
faq.answer: The Horde needs Ashenvale's timber to build and hold its home in Kalimdor. The Warsong Mill at the gulch is one of its main sources, and the Outriders defend it so the Horde's camps and walls can rise.

faq.q: Why do the night elves fight in Warsong Gulch?
faq.answer: The night elves have guarded sacred Ashenvale for ten thousand years, and the Warsong clan once slew the demigod Cenarius there. The Silverwing Sentinels fight to stop the logging and drive the orcs from their woods, with the rest of the Alliance beside them.

The Warsong Outriders are the Horde's fighters in Warsong Gulch, drawn from the Warsong clan once led by Grom Hellscream. They receive supplies at Mor'shan Base Camp in the northern Barrens, where Kelm Hargunth equips them.

The Silverwing Sentinels are night elf warriors of Silverwing Hold, sworn to drive the Horde from Ashenvale. At Silverwing Grove, Illiyana Moonblaze supplies the Alliance champions who fight beside them in the gulch.

faq.q: How is the battle in Warsong Gulch won?
faq.answer: Each side keeps its flag in its own stronghold. Fighters raid the enemy's hold, seize its flag and carry it home while defending their own banner. The side that brings home the most flags wins.

angles.text: Every log from the Warsong Mill helps raise a Horde wall somewhere in Kalimdor. Hold the gulch, and the Horde can keep building.
Alliance soldiers fight beside their night elf allies as the Warsong clan's axes bring down trees in their sacred forest.
These woods have known kaldorei feet for ten thousand years. Every orc driven from the gulch is a piece of Ashenvale won back.
The Warsong clan is Grom Hellscream's own. In the gulch, his warriors still earn their name with axe in hand against the Sentinels.
